metadata.case_name: TALAT ARSLAN v. LI TAK CHEUNG

manifestations.description: right sided headache once a week which lasted for an hour or so each time
pain in the left finger when holding heavy objects or wringing a towel
continuous low back pain which intensified to grade 8-9/10 when sitting from more than half an hour or lying in bed for long periods
intermittent pain in the left hip at grade 7-8/10 particularly during cold and humid weather, walking for over 10 minutes or climbing stairs
unable to make a full squat, or to walk on tiptoes or heels
unable to stand on his left leg
23 cm long scar extending from L1 to S2 level of the spine with tenderness at the surrounding areas
1 cm scar to the left of the scrotum similarly with tenderness at the nearby region

Mr Arslan demonstrated substantial limitation in the flexion of the spine. Straight leg raising while sitting was 90 degrees on the right side but 70 degrees on the left side. There was also a decreased range of movement of the hip on the left with slight muscle wasting of the thigh and calf.
mild bony swelling and tenderness over the dorsum of the proximal phalanx, however, the range of movement was found to be normal

treatments_received.treatment: open reduction with internal fixation of the spine
source: an open reduction with internal fixation was performed at Mr Arslan’s spine.

treatments_received.treatment: closed reduction with internal fixation of the pelvis
source: The fracture at his pelvis was treated by way of closed reduction with internal fixation.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Closed reduction for fracture of arm / leg / patella / pelvis with internal fixation

treatments_received.treatment: removal of metal implant at the spine
source: In October 2014, the metal implant at the spine was removed.
he received physiotherapy and occupational therapy.
he received physiotherapy and occupational therapy.
As back pain persisted, Mr Arslan was readmitted to the Tuen Mun Hospital to receive an injection.

losses.description: multiple scars over his right face and both elbows; 23 cm long scar extending from L1 to S2 level of the spine; 1 cm scar to the left of the scrotum
unable to make a full squat, unable to walk on tiptoes or heels, unable to stand on his left leg, decreased range of movement of the left hip, limited flexion of the spine
closed fracture of the left acetabulum, fracture of the lumbar spine at L2/L3, dislocation at L5/S1, fracture of proximal phalanx of the left ring finger and the surgical interventions that followed
